an So durchl.
daß er seit anderthalb Jahren vom 4 May 1803. bis 4 Nov. a. c.
einen Zins Rükstand von 5572 Rthl 12. gg. an Sr Durchl. habe zu
fordern, er hätte geglaubt, daß da Trąbczyn, admiuhträt
wurde er zu s. Zahlung gelangen würde, er habe deshalb ein
Mandat bey Kalischer Regierung bewirbt, welches Sr. d. binnen 14
Tagen die Zahlung auflegt, wundert sich aber, daß diese ver¬
strichen und er nichts erhalten habe. Er droht mit Antrag auf
sequestration will abwägerne Sr. durchl. Verdruß erspa¬
ren und wünscht fernerhin in gutem Vernehmen zu stehen
und glaubt daß die Weihnachten Selittel bringen wurden
ihr zu befriedigen.
Antwort.
die Pächter hätten nicht gezahlt — er würde befriedigt werden, da
Herr v. Triebenfeld dort alles in Ordnung und ins Reine brächta
d. 27ten Nov. 1804

translation.en: The Provincial Elder v. Lichnowski 11. writes, dated 23 Nov. 1804, to His Serene Highness, that for the past year and a half, from 4 May 1803 to 4 Nov. of the current year, he has to demand from His Serene Highness an arrears of interest of 5572 Rthl 12 Groschen; he had believed that, since Trąbczyn was being administered, he would obtain his payment; he had therefore procured a mandate from the Kalisch Government, which imposes payment upon His Serene Highness within 14 days, but he is astonished that these have elapsed and he has received nothing. He threatens with an application for sequestration, wishes [uncertain: abwägerne] to spare His Serene Highness vexation, and desires to continue on good terms, and believes that Christmas would bring the means to satisfy him. Answer: the tenants had not paid — he would be satisfied, since Herr v. Triebenfeld was putting everything there in order and in the clear. The 27th of Nov. 1804

text_english: The Provincial Elder v. Lichnowski 11. writes, dated 23 Nov. 1804, to His Serene Highness, that for the past year and a half, from 4 May 1803 to 4 Nov. of the current year, he has to demand from His Serene Highness an arrears of interest of 5572 Rthl 12 Groschen; he had believed that, since Trąbczyn was being administered, he would obtain his payment; he had therefore procured a mandate from the Kalisch Government, which imposes payment upon His Serene Highness within 14 days, but he is astonished that these have elapsed and he has received nothing. He threatens with an application for sequestration, wishes [uncertain: abwägerne] to spare His Serene Highness vexation, and desires to continue on good terms, and believes that Christmas would bring the means to satisfy him. Answer: the tenants had not paid — he would be satisfied, since Herr v. Triebenfeld was putting everything there in order and in the clear. The 27th of Nov. 1804
summary_en: Reports a letter of 23 November 1804 from Provincial Elder v. Lichnowski demanding 5572 Rthl 12 Groschen in interest arrears accrued from 4 May 1803 to 4 November 1804; expecting payment from the administered Trąbczyn, he obtained a mandate from the Kalisch Government setting a fourteen-day term, now expired, and threatens to apply for sequestration while professing goodwill and hoping for settlement at Christmas. The reply pleads unpaid tenants and v. Triebenfeld's ongoing regulation of affairs.
summary_de: Der Landesälteste v. Lichnowski fordert für anderthalb Jahre, vom 4. Mai 1803 bis 4. Nov. 1804, rückständige Zinsen von 5572 Rthl 12 Groschen; er hatte auf Zahlung aus der Administration von Trąbczyn gehofft und ein Mandat der Kalischer Regierung erwirkt, das Zahlung binnen 14 Tagen auferlegte, doch nach fruchtlosem Ablauf droht er mit dem Antrag auf Sequestration, will jedoch Verdruß ersparen und erwartet Befriedigung zu Weihnachten. Antwort vom 27. Nov. 1804: die Pächter hätten nicht gezahlt, Herr v. Triebenfeld bringe alles in Ordnung.
